about.title: Lafayette Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Lafayette's mix of downtown shops, office parks, and residential complexes near corridors like SR-24 means plenty of foot traffic on stairways, parking lots, and walkways owned by someone else. When a property owner lets a hazard go unaddressed — a wet floor, broken step, uneven pavement, or poor lighting — and someone gets hurt, California law may hold them responsible, but only if it can be shown they knew or reasonably should have known about the danger and didn't fix it or warn visitors. That's why documenting the scene matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage can disappear or get overwritten within days. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect Lafayette residents and visitors who've been injured with an independent attorney who can evaluate the notice issue, gather evidence before it's lost, and explain your options. The consultation is free, and there's no cost unless the attorney recovers something for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Speak With an Attorney Early

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California premises cases hinge on proving the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can start building that record right away, before memories fade.

items.title: Video Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many Lafayette businesses recycle surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: Because California uses pure comparative fault, you can still recover even if you were partly careless, but the property owner's side will try to shift blame onto you. Early legal guidance helps counter that.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Lafayette?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned — say, a public sidewalk or a Contra Costa County building — that window shrinks dramatically and requires an earlier claim filing. An attorney can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I fell but wasn't sure what caused it?
items.answer: That's common — people often don't realize what they slipped on until afterward. An independent attorney can help investigate, pull incident reports, and request video from the property to piece together what happened. Waiting too long makes that evidence harder to get.

items.question: Does it matter that my fall happened near a busy area like SR-24?
items.answer: Not directly — premises liability is about the property owner's conduct, not traffic patterns. But businesses along high-traffic corridors near SR-24 in Lafayette often have more foot traffic and more surveillance cameras, which can actually help establish what happened.

items.question: Will I owe anything if I talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to have your situation reviewed.
